questions.question: Let $f(x)=1+\sqrt{x}$. What is the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$?
questions.answer: $f$ has domain $x\ge0$ and range $y\ge1$; the inverse swaps these.

questions.question: What is the size of the acute angle, to the nearest degree, between $\underset{\sim}{u}=\begin{pmatrix}\sqrt3\\2\end{pmatrix}$ and $\underset{\sim}{v}=\begin{pmatrix}9\\\sqrt{17}\end{pmatrix}$?
Which of the following is the solution to $\dfrac{3}{x-2}\le4$?
Let $f(x)=\tan^{-1}(\tan x)$. What is the value of $f\left(\dfrac{9\pi}{4}\right)$?
A polynomial $P(x)$ leaves a remainder of $n^2$ when divided by $(x+1)$, where $n$ is a positive integer. When $P(x)$ is divided by $(x+1)(x+3)$, the remainder is $nx+6$. What is the value of $n$?
Which of the following is equal to $\int\sin3x\sin x\,dx$?
The graph of $y=P'(x)$ is shown below. $P(x)$ is a polynomial of degree 4 and has a multiple root. Which statement about $P(x)$ is true?
questions.answer: $P'$ has a double root at $x=2$, so if $P(2)=0$ it is a triple root. $x=-1$ is only a simple root of $P'$ and $P'(0)\ne0$.

questions.question: What is the derivative of $2x^2\cos^{-1}(2x)$?
Let $f(x)=\dfrac{1}{x-2}+2$. The graph of $y=g(x)$, obtained by applying transformations to $y=f(x)$, is shown below. Which of the following is a possible expression for $g(x)$?
The projection of $\underset{\sim}{a}$ onto $\underset{\sim}{b}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\6\end{pmatrix}$ is $\frac12\underset{\sim}{b}$. Which of the following is a possible vector $\underset{\sim}{a}$?
Consider the point $P(12,5)$. Write the position vector of $P$ and a unit vector in the direction of the position vector.
Find $\displaystyle\int\sin^2\left(\frac{2x}{3}\right)dx$.
Using $t$-formulae, solve $2\sin x+\cos x+1=0$ for $0\le x\le2\pi$.
questions.answer:
With $t=\tan\frac x2$ (for $x\ne\pi$):
$$\frac{4t}{1+t^2}+\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}+1=0\Rightarrow 4t+2=0\Rightarrow t=-\tfrac12$$
$\dfrac x2=\pi-\tan^{-1}\tfrac12$, so $x=2\pi-2\tan^{-1}\tfrac12\approx5.356$.

Check $x=\pi$: $0-1+1=0$, so it is also a solution.

Therefore $x=\pi$ or $x\approx5.356$.

questions.question: Find $\displaystyle\int\frac{dx}{\sqrt{64-49x^2}}$.
Express $\cos x-\sqrt3\sin x$ in the form $R\cos(x+\alpha)$.
Hence, or otherwise, solve $\cos x-\sqrt3\sin x=2$ for $x$ in the interval $[0,2\pi]$.
Four teams of two tennis players are to be seated at a circular table. In how many ways can they be seated if the two players of each team sit together?
questions.answer:
Arrange the 4 team blocks in a circle in $3!$ ways, and order each pair in $2$ ways:
$$3!\times2^4=96$$

questions.question: Use the substitution $x=\sin\theta$ to evaluate $\displaystyle\int_0^{1/2}\frac{dx}{(1-x^2)^{3/2}}$.
Prove by mathematical induction that $3^{3n-1}+5^{3n-2}$ is divisible by 7 for all positive integers $n$.
questions.answer:
**$n=1$:** $3^2+5^1=14=7\times2$. True.

**Assume** true for $n=k$: $3^{3k-1}+5^{3k-2}=7P$ for an integer $P$.

**$n=k+1$:**
$$3^{3k+2}+5^{3k+1}=27\cdot3^{3k-1}+125\cdot5^{3k-2}$$
$$=27\left(7P-5^{3k-2}\right)+125\cdot5^{3k-2}$$
$$=189P+98\cdot5^{3k-2}=7\left(27P+14\cdot5^{3k-2}\right)$$
which is divisible by 7. Hence true for all positive integers $n$ by induction.

questions.question: A cake tin cools according to $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-k(T-R)$, where $T$ is its temperature, $R$ is room temperature, $t$ is the time in minutes and $k$ is a constant. The solution is $T=R+Ae^{-kt}$ (do NOT prove this). The tin is taken from an oven at $180^\circ$C into a room at $20^\circ$C, and after one minute it is $150^\circ$C. How long, to the nearest minute, will it take for the tin to reach $80^\circ$C?
questions.answer:
$R=20$ and $T(0)=180$, so $A=160$.

$T(1)=150$: $130=160e^{-k}\Rightarrow e^{-k}=\dfrac{13}{16}$.

$80=20+160\left(\dfrac{13}{16}\right)^t\Rightarrow\left(\dfrac{13}{16}\right)^t=\dfrac38$
$$t=\frac{\ln(3/8)}{\ln(13/16)}\approx4.72$$
It takes about 5 minutes.

questions.question: An equilateral triangle has side length $x$ metres. The side length is shrinking at a rate of $\sqrt{x}$ metres per second. Show that the rate of change of its area is $\dfrac{dA}{dt}=-\dfrac{\sqrt3\,x\sqrt x}{2}$ m²/s.

An equilateral triangle has side length $x$ metres. The side length is shrinking at a rate of $\sqrt{x}$ metres per second. A circle, of radius $r$ metres, always has the same area as the triangle. At what rate, correct to 2 decimal places, is the radius of the circle changing when $x=5$?
questions.answer:
$\pi r^2=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{4}x^2\Rightarrow r=\dfrac{3^{1/4}}{2\sqrt\pi}x$.
$$\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac{3^{1/4}}{2\sqrt\pi}\cdot\frac{dx}{dt}=-\frac{3^{1/4}\sqrt x}{2\sqrt\pi}$$
At $x=5$: $\dfrac{dr}{dt}\approx-0.83$ m/s, so the radius is decreasing at about $0.83$ m/s.

questions.question: By considering the expansion of $(1+x)^{2n}+(1-x)^{2n}$, show that $$1+\binom{2n}{2}+\binom{2n}{4}+\dots+\binom{2n}{2n}=\frac{4^n}{2}.$$
questions.answer:
Odd powers cancel:
$$(1+x)^{2n}+(1-x)^{2n}=2\left[1+\binom{2n}{2}x^2+\binom{2n}{4}x^4+\dots+\binom{2n}{2n}x^{2n}\right]$$
Put $x=1$: LHS $=2^{2n}=4^n$. Dividing by 2 gives the result.

questions.question: $OABC$ is a trapezium with $\overrightarrow{OA}=3\overrightarrow{CB}$. $E$ and $F$ are the midpoints of the diagonals $OB$ and $CA$. Let $\overrightarrow{OA}=\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\underset{\sim}{c}$. Show that $\overrightarrow{OE}=\dfrac12\left(\underset{\sim}{c}+\dfrac13\underset{\sim}{a}\right)$.

$OABC$ is a trapezium with $\overrightarrow{OA}=3\overrightarrow{CB}$. $E$ and $F$ are the midpoints of the diagonals $OB$ and $CA$. Let $\overrightarrow{OA}=\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\underset{\sim}{c}$. Find $\overrightarrow{EF}$.

$OABC$ is a trapezium with $\overrightarrow{OA}=3\overrightarrow{CB}$. $E$ and $F$ are the midpoints of the diagonals $OB$ and $CA$. Let $\overrightarrow{OA}=\underset{\sim}{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{OC}=\underset{\sim}{c}$. Prove that $CEFB$ is a parallelogram.
questions.answer: $\overrightarrow{EF}=\frac13\underset{\sim}{a}=\overrightarrow{CB}$. So $EF$ and $CB$ are equal and parallel; a quadrilateral with one pair of opposite sides equal and parallel is a parallelogram.

questions.question: A particle moves in a straight line, starting at $x=0$ when $t=0$, with velocity $v=\dfrac{e^t}{1+(e^t)^2}$ (graph shown). Its displacement at $t=k$ is $\tan^{-1}\dfrac12$. Show that $k=\ln3$.

Jacob hits two balls at the same time from $O$ towards a target on a vertical wall. Ball 1 has initial speed $V$ at angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal; ball 2 has initial speed $\dfrac{15V}{7}$ at angle $2\alpha$. Using integration, show that the position vector of ball 2 is $$\underset{\sim}{r_2}(t)=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{15V}{7}t\cos2\alpha\\-\frac12gt^2+\frac{15V}{7}t\sin2\alpha\end{pmatrix}.$$
questions.answer:
$\underset{\sim}{a}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\-g\end{pmatrix}$. Integrating and using $\underset{\sim}{v}(0)=\frac{15V}{7}\begin{pmatrix}\cos2\alpha\\\sin2\alpha\end{pmatrix}$:
$$\underset{\sim}{v}(t)=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{15V}{7}\cos2\alpha\\-gt+\frac{15V}{7}\sin2\alpha\end{pmatrix}$$
Integrating again with $\underset{\sim}{r}(0)=\underset{\sim}{0}$ gives the required $\underset{\sim}{r_2}(t)$.

questions.question: Jacob hits two balls at the same time from $O$ towards a target on a vertical wall. Ball 1 has initial speed $V$ at angle $\alpha$ to the horizontal; ball 2 has initial speed $\dfrac{15V}{7}$ at angle $2\alpha$. The position vector of ball 2 is $\underset{\sim}{r_2}(t)=\left(\frac{15V}{7}t\cos2\alpha,\ -\frac12gt^2+\frac{15V}{7}t\sin2\alpha\right)$. Both balls hit the wall after $T$ seconds. Show that $\cos\alpha=\dfrac56$.
questions.answer:
Both have the same horizontal displacement at $t=T$:
$$VT\cos\alpha=\frac{15V}{7}T\cos2\alpha$$
$$7\cos\alpha=15(2\cos^2\alpha-1)$$
$$30\cos^2\alpha-7\cos\alpha-15=0$$
$$(6\cos\alpha-5)(5\cos\alpha+3)=0$$
$\alpha$ is acute so $\cos\alpha>0$, hence $\cos\alpha=\dfrac56$.

questions.question: The region bounded by the line $y=2x-1$, the parabola $y=(x-2)^2$ and the $y$-axis (shaded) is rotated about the $y$-axis. The line and parabola meet at $A(1,1)$. Find the volume of the solid formed.
questions.answer:
For $-1\le y\le1$ the radius is $x=\dfrac{y+1}{2}$; for $1\le y\le4$ it is $x=2-\sqrt y$.
$$V=\pi\int_{-1}^1\frac{(y+1)^2}{4}dy+\pi\int_1^4(4-4\sqrt y+y)\,dy$$
$$=\pi\left[\frac{(y+1)^3}{12}\right]_{-1}^1+\pi\left[4y-\frac83y^{3/2}+\frac{y^2}{2}\right]_1^4$$
$$=\frac{2\pi}{3}+\frac{5\pi}{6}=\frac{3\pi}{2}\text{ units}^3$$

questions.question: Show that the solution to $\cos3x-\sin2x=0$ for $0<x<\dfrac\pi2$ is given by $\sin x=\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{4}$. (You may use $\cos3x=4\cos^3x-3\cos x$.)
questions.answer:
$$4\cos^3x-3\cos x-2\sin x\cos x=0$$
$$\cos x\left(4\cos^2x-3-2\sin x\right)=0$$
$\cos x\ne0$ on the interval, so $4(1-\sin^2x)-3-2\sin x=0$, i.e. $4\sin^2x+2\sin x-1=0$.
$$\sin x=\frac{-1\pm\sqrt5}{4}$$
$\sin x>0$, so $\sin x=\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{4}$.

questions.question: Without using a calculator, verify that $x=\dfrac\pi{10}$ satisfies $\cos3x=\sin2x$.
Given that the solution of $\cos3x=\sin2x$ in $0<x<\dfrac\pi2$ is $x=\dfrac{\pi}{10}$, with $\sin x=\dfrac{\sqrt5-1}{4}$, prove that $\sin\dfrac\pi5\cos\dfrac\pi{10}=\dfrac{\sqrt5}{4}$.
